Indicators that rose or fell between two years for one country

Source: R/fct_change.R
indicator_change.Rd

Compares every indicator a country has a value for in both years and splits them into two tables: the ones that increased from year1 to year2 and the ones that decreased, each sorted by percent change (largest change first). Percent change is (value2 - value1) / |value1| * 100; it is undefined when the year1 value is 0, so those indicators are left out of both tables (their names are kept in the zero_base element). Indicators that did not change are in neither table.

Usage

indicator_change(
  mfi,
  country,
  year1,
  year2,
  include_rates = FALSE,
  include_sign_change = FALSE
)

Arguments

mfi

Data frame of World Bank indicator values (long format, with Country Name, Indicator Name, Year, value columns).

country

Character. Country name, as in Country Name.

year1, year2

Numeric or character. The two years to compare.

include_rates

Logical. Keep the rate-of-change indicators (names containing "annual %", "% change" or "growth"); FALSE (default) leaves them out.

include_sign_change

Logical. Keep indicators whose value changed sign between the two years (e.g. net FDI inflows from -8 million to +6.7 billion): their percent change is not meaningful (+82,000%). FALSE (default) leaves them out and lists them in sign_change.

Value

A list with increased and decreased (data frames with columns Indicator, the two years' values, Change and Change %), zero_base (indicators left out because their year1 value is 0) and sign_change (indicators whose value changed sign; left out unless include_sign_change = TRUE).

Details

Rates of change ("annual %", "% change", "growth", e.g. "GDP growth (annual %)", "Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)", "... (% change from 1990)") are left out by default: a percent change of a growth rate is not meaningful (a rate going from -0.01 to 1.7 reads as +17,000%). include_rates = TRUE keeps them.

For indicators that are themselves percentages (e.g. "Urban population (% of total population)") the percent change is relative to the old percentage, not a difference in percentage points; the Change column gives the plain difference.

Examples

res <- indicator_change(mfi, country = "Greece", year1 = 2024, year2 = 2025)
head(res$increased)
#>                                                    Indicator         2024         2025       Change Change %
#> 1 Foreign direct investment, net outflows (BoP, current US$) 2.219862e+09 5.957093e+09 3.737232e+09   168.35
#> 2         Foreign direct investment, net outflows (% of GDP) 8.663269e-01 2.122715e+00 1.256389e+00   145.02
#> 3                   Stocks traded, total value (current US$) 2.323616e+10 4.811845e+10 2.488229e+10   107.08
#> 4  Foreign direct investment, net inflows (BoP, current US$) 6.742277e+09 1.357470e+10 6.832427e+09   101.34
#> 5                      Stocks traded, total value (% of GDP) 9.068181e+00 1.714624e+01 8.078062e+00    89.08
#> 6          Foreign direct investment, net inflows (% of GDP) 2.631252e+00 4.837130e+00 2.205878e+00    83.83
head(res$decreased)
#>                                           Indicator        2024         2025      Change Change %
#> 1      Portfolio investment, net (BoP, current US$) -6325496155 -12777283277 -6451787122  -102.00
#> 2       Arms exports (SIPRI trend indicator values)    20000000      2000000   -18000000   -90.00
#> 3              Changes in inventories (current LCU)  5333733000    900044000 -4433689000   -83.13
#> 4              Changes in inventories (current US$)  5773128425   1017034543 -4756093882   -82.38
#> 5 Foreign direct investment, net (BoP, current US$) -4522415327  -7617610888 -3095195560   -68.44
